subject: Request: ServePolicy override for MediaCorp (geo pin + no-fallback)
messages:
From: Anna Liao <anna.liao@mediacorp.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: ServePolicy override request: geo pin + no-fallback for MediaCorp Prod

Hi Mina,

Quick one — our security team has a hard requirement that all inference for MediaCorp's production tenant be served from the us-east region and that there can be no fallback to lower-cost model families (even during transient capacity pressure). The ask is two-fold:

1) Geo pinning: route all traffic for our tenant to us-east only.
2) No-fallback: if the primary model is unavailable, fail requests rather than falling back to a smaller/quantized variant.

They say the reasons are regulatory traceability and a requirement that model architecture + weights be strictly controlled for audit traces. We understand that this impacts availability and may affect SLOs. Attached is MediaCorp's SOC2 summary and a draft mutual action plan showing the compliance milestones.

Can Redwood provide a short write-up of technical limitations/risks and a temp exception path if we need to grant this (e.g., limited-duration override with operational guardrails)? We need something to present to their infosec and procurement tomorrow.

Thanks,
Anna
Anna Liao
Head of Platform Security, MediaCorp

Immediate asks:
- Product (Lauren): Can you outline product-level implications (config surfaces, monitoring changes, whether we can gate this behind a per-tenant flag)?
- Infra (Karthik): What are the runtime constraints for implementing a region-only routing and disabling fallback? How fast can we roll this safely for a single tenant?
- SRE/Platform (Connor): If we grant a temporary override, what operational guardrails (circuit-breakers, rate-limits, automatic rollback) should be required?

I copied Anna so they see we're on it. Please reply with concrete options and suggested wording we can share with MediaCorp infosec. Time sensitive — they want materials tomorrow EOD.

Thanks,
Mina

Subject: Re: Fwd: ServePolicy override request: geo pin + no-fallback for MediaCorp Prod

Thanks for the ping. High-level product implications:

- Per-tenant routing config: we already support region preferences for routing, but hard geo-pin (no cross-region fallback) is currently not an exposed self-serve toggle — it would be a config change in the routing policy.
- No-fallback semantics: currently our fallback layer prefers compatible model variants to preserve availability. Turning off fallback means failed calls during capacity pressure; can be surfaced as 503s.
- Auditability: we can record model/host assignment in the trace and add extra retention for the tenant's traces for audit purposes. That adds small storage/cost.

Options to propose to MediaCorp:
A) Strict: apply geo-pin + disable fallback. Pros: meets their requirement. Cons: higher outage risk, requires manual approvals and extended monitoring.
B) Soft guarantee with attestation: geo-pin + allow fallback to pre-approved model artifacts only (we'd restrict to a vetted list of compatible weights). Pros: better availability, still auditable. Cons: requires onboarding/validation of fallback artifacts.
C) Time-boxed override: start with Soft guarantee for a 30-day window while legal & infosec complete their audit, with an option to escalate to Strict if they insist.

Suggested wording for their infosec: a one-page summary of the expected availability impact and recommended guardrails (circuit breaker, higher alerting, two-person ops approval for deploys). I can draft that now if you want.

-Lauren
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Fwd: ServePolicy override request: geo pin + no-fallback for MediaCorp Prod

Quick infra read:

- Geo-pin to us-east only: straightforward at the routing plane (policy change). We'll need capacity reservations or a dedicated shard for them to avoid noisy-neighbor impact. If we do a soft pin (preferred only), traffic can still route elsewhere during extreme conditions — strict pin prevents that.
- Disabling fallback: requires disabling the fallback switch in the model selection service for their tenant. That's low-risk from a code change perspective, but it means any upstream congestion or degraded hosts will surface client-visible failures.
- Rollout approach I'd recommend:
  1) Staging proof: mirror traffic to a us-east-only pool for 48 hours, confirm latencies and queue/backpressure behavior.
  2) Capacity reservation: allocate a small dedicated pool with autoscale but reserved baseline.
  3) Feature flag: flip no-fallback behind a tenant-scoped flag, enable it for a small percentage of requests (5%) for 24 hours, then increase to 100% if stable.

We can deliver a short ops runbook for on-call and a canned rollback (re-enable fallback or un-pin) — should be < 4 hours to execute.

-Karthik
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: anna.liao@mediacorp.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ServePolicy override request: geo pin + no-fallback for MediaCorp Prod

Anna — thanks for the quick turnaround. We're aligned on a safe path forward and can present this to MediaCorp infosec/procurement:

Proposal summary (to share externally):
- Phase 1 (Audit-ready, low disruption): enable geo-pin to us-east AND allow fallback only to a pre-approved set of model artifacts (Option B above). We'll retain traces and increase retention for audit. We'll also require a 7-day capacity reservation baseline.
- Phase 2 (Strict, if required): after MediaCorp validation and a joint operational readiness review, we can enable strict no-fallback + hard geo-pin for production for a time-boxed 90-day pilot. This will require a signed exception (legal sign-off) and a dedicated ops runbook with two-person approval to change the flag.

Operational guardrails we will enforce for any override:
- Circuit breaker: automatic fail-open to 503s after sustained queue > threshold.
- Alerting: dedicated on-call for MediaCorp with 15m SLA for initial triage during pilot.
- Rollback: a single CLI command to re-enable fallback and remove geo-pin; tested in staging weekly.

Next steps:
1) Anna: confirm that MediaCorp is okay starting with Phase 1 (geo-pin + vetted fallback artifacts) and sign the mutual action plan we received.
2) Mina/Redwood: we'll produce a 1-page technical risks doc + an ops runbook and send both by EOD tomorrow.
3) Legal: if they insist on Phase 2 now, we will need a signed exception and SOC2 evidence; please confirm.

If helpful, Lauren will attach the 1-pager and Karthik will attach the rollout checklist.

Thanks — Mina
